result:
The validator was right and I was wrong. I verified the error myself before fixing it.

## The false claim, measured false

I asserted a mechanism I never measured: that an all-zero source row ties all 21 candidates, so cold queries score at chance 1/21. `tie_check.py` trained the embedding and looked at the actual scores:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| cold source rows actually all-zero | **216/216** — that part of my premise was right |
| cold queries with all 21 scores tied | **0/216** (median 20 distinct; spread 2.12–5.33) |
| tiebreak varies between runs | **No** — `evaluate_ranking` is never passed a seed, so it's byte-identical and contributes zero variance |
| reproduces ×15 seed-0 cold value | **0.0880**, exact |
| is 0.0803 at chance? | **No** — chance is 0.0476; observed is +2.8 binomial sd above it |

**Why:** with `u=0`, the hadamard/dot/cos features collapse to constants, but `|u−v|` and `‖u−v‖` reduce to `|v|` and `‖v‖`, which vary by candidate. The predictor ranks cold queries on candidate-only features — a popularity prior, not chance.

Your self-disproving argument is the one that stings: tied scores plus a constant tiebreak would force *identical* cold hit@1 at every seed, yet mine differ (0.0880/0.0972/0.0556). That was sitting in my own results table and I didn't check it. I built an elegant-sounding mechanism and never tested it, in the same round I was congratulating myself for testing the control at the root.

## Fixes

- **Cold-start paragraph** re-anchored on the measured token-matched control: **3.5× / 4.5×** (gaps **7.5 / 10.3** cold-bucket sd), replacing "5.9× / 7.6× chance" (8.7 / 11.5). All regenerated by `make_tables.py`, which now carries a comment recording why chance is *not* the anchor.
- Added one sentence that is now actually measured — the floor sits above chance because of the candidate-only features, 0/216 tied.
- **Removed the `chance (1/21)` line from both figures**; regenerated, re-rendered, looked at them, and confirmed neither PDF contains the string "chance".
- Conclusion → "by 3.5–4.5× over a budget-matched baseline"; density paragraph → "ranked on a popularity prior".
- **`float` removed** — and I checked the rest the same way rather than fixing only what you named: `amssymb` and `caption` were also unused. Preamble is down to **5 lines**, each verified necessary by deleting it and confirming the compile fails.
- `submission.md` rewritten; the wrong justification is gone, and the round-2 caveat that explained the 0.0494/0.0803 control gap as "tie-breaking noise" now says what it actually is — genuine seed-to-seed variance in the learned embedding.

Still 6 pages, no bad boxes, 0 undefined refs, lint clean, R5 clean, 21/21 table rows traced.

The cold-start result itself is unchanged — 0.2824/0.3596 against a 0.0803 baseline is still the largest effect in the study. Only the anchor and the mechanism were wrong.
